scope: Specified internal E-alkene acid and sulfonamide with adamantan-1-ol/TfOH/HFIP; balanced intermediate, TS, local-barrier and product free energies, plus a validated trans-forming pathway.
guidance_markdown:
# Author hypothesis and method baseline

The authors model the public acid and sulfonamide as 1a and 1s, adamantan-1-ol as 2a, and the trans products as 3a and 3s. Their hypothesis is TfOH-assisted exchange of adamantanol with HFIP to form the adamantyl HFIP ether, water release, ionization to the 1-adamantyl cation plus triflate with HFIP release, then electrophilic cyclization and deprotonation. The reported cyclization transition structures combine substrate and adamantyl cation with the acidic O-H/N-H proton retained, and contain no explicit triflate or HFIP. The proposed cyclization couples C-C bond formation and ring closure. Test these states and connections; no energy ordering or favored substrate is supplied.

The reported baseline uses Gaussian 16, B3LYP/def2-TZVP geometry optimizations and harmonic frequencies, and M06/def2-TZVP single points, with SMD HFIP at 293.15 K. HFIP uses dielectric constant 16.70 with all other solvent parameters copied from 2-propanol. Profiles specify pressure 1 atm. Stationary-point classification uses zero imaginary frequencies for minima and one for a transition structure. Verify the chemical connection of a claimed TS with an IRC or justified equivalent evidence.

The SI energy table separates solvent M06 electronic energies from B3LYP thermal corrections labeled gas phase; the methods prose describes optimization in solvent. Record this unresolved thermochemistry implementation detail and declare your reconstruction. Low-frequency processing, standard-state changes beyond the printed pressure, grids and convergence thresholds are not supplied instructions. The coordinate/energy tables are available in SI Tables S21/S22. Software substitutions are allowed with their consequences explained.

Use an atom-, proton- and charge-balanced free-energy ledger. For substrate X, one convenient initial reference is AdOH + X + TfOH + HFIP. The ether level contains Ad-O-CH(CF3)2 + X + H2O + TfOH; the ionized level contains Ad+ + X + OTf- + H2O + HFIP; the cyclization TS level contains the proton-retaining [Ad+X]+ TS + OTf- + H2O + HFIP; and the product level contains neutral product + TfOH + H2O + HFIP. These choices keep the same atoms and net charge. Closed-shell charge assignments follow the depicted chemistry: Ad+ and cyclization TS +1, OTf- -1, other isolated species neutral. The source summary does not print all input charge/multiplicity lines; declare and validate the actual settings.

A local cyclization barrier is the TS free energy minus the separated carbocation-plus-substrate level, distinct from the height of that TS on the full alcohol-based profile. Ether and cation formation energies are intermediate thermodynamics; the source supplies no activation TSs for those formation steps. The source models trans pathways and does not supply a competing cis TS for this substrate pair. Do not turn that absence into an additional mandatory calculation or a quantitative trans/cis prediction. The author mechanism is a testable hypothesis, not an answer to repeat.
status: Disclosed methods and hypotheses only; author result values and ordering are private.
